newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves MMTC plans on steel plant.
newsitem.headline: India approves MMTC plans on steel plant.

text.p: The Indian cabinet has cleared a proposal by the state-run trading corp MMTC Ltd to set up a $422 million steel plant with private investors in the eastern state of Orissa, MMTC officials said on Tuesday.
"The proposal was cleared by the cabinet recently," S.N. Malik, MMTC chairman and managing director told reporters.
Malik said the plant Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL), to be set up at an estimated cost of 15.10 billion rupees ($422 million), would produce 1.1 million tonnes of steel annually.
"It is expected that the blast furnace will commence production in 27 months from the zero date, which is April, 1997," a company statement said.

MMTC would contribute an equity investment of one billion rupees towards the project cost and the remaining would be held by state-run agencies, private domestic and foreign investors, the statement said.

The Commonwealth Development Corp of London would provide an equity investment of 530 million rupees, while South Korea's Lucky Goldstar would extend equity of 770 million rupees for the project, the statement said.
Malik said about 2.45 billion rupees would be raised through a public issue by NINL, but gave no timeframe.
About 9.07 billion rupees would be provided by domestic financial institutions as term loans, Malik said.
Malik said a plant to supply coke and power to the steel plant would be also set up near NINL at an estimated cost of 4.8 billion rupees, of which MMTC would provide 490 million. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
